crime_highlights: The accused had a firearm which looked like a 303 rifle.
He fired it in the air and asked the complainants if they wanted to die today.
He then approached the complainants and pointed the firearm at them.
The accused walked towards McKinnon Charlie, put the rifle next to his ear and then pulled the trigger.
McKinnon Charlie developed headaches and intermittent ringing in his ear and had difficult hearing for some time.
rationale_highlights: The bands were all forced together and remained that way for a number of years.
the jurisprudence indicates that I could and should consider a conditional sentence in a case like this
I intend to impose a fine and a conditional sentence on the accused for these offences
note: Court never ties Indigenous background to culpability; conditional sentence based on rehabilitation.

crime_highlights: he reached across and touched the complainant on the leg and breasts and kissed her

rationale_highlights: the trial judge sitting in judgment of the long-serving chief of this small native band was much better placed than is this court in assessing and measuring the significance to that community of the various sentencing options
may well have had a greater denunciatory and general deterrence effect in his small aboriginal community than it would have in a larger non-aboriginal community
an aboriginal offender's community will frequently understand the nature of a just sanction in a manner significantly different from that of many non-aboriginal communities
note: Appeal court upholds short sentence citing community understanding of sanction.
